reasoning_traces.think:
The Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) model defines win probabilities through logistic link function ψ(t) = e^t/(1+e^t). Maximum likelihood estimation yields θ̂ by maximizing log-likelihood over pairwise comparisons. Spectral estimation constructs a Markov transition matrix from adjacency and outcomes, then extracts stationary distribution to estimate θ̃. Both methods assume ER random graph structure with bounded dynamic range κ = O(1). Asymptotic theory ensures consistency and normality of estimators under np ≫ (log n)^α. Confidence intervals are constructed using estimated standard errors, enabling probabilistic rank inference. However, these approaches lack temporal dynamics, margin-of-victory modeling, and do not account for covariates like home field advantage or rest. Their applicability to real-world sports depends on extrapolating from simulation results to actual datasets such as NFL schedules.
